proof:
# Actual source endpoints restrict affine scale, but do not remove every jump

This lemma uses actual deepestness, unlike the geometry-only affine
minorant counterexamples. It retains the finite-epsilon buffer error.
The exact integer calculation in Section 2 only tests the resulting
necessary numerical condition; it does not construct an H-stationary
configuration.

## 1. Source-endpoint inequality

Let n=1. Assume an actual propagated envelope

    K_z subset y(z)+ell(z)D

with positive affine ell, and equality on a deepest-source interval
[a,b], where a,b are integers and b-a=m>=2.
Assume ell is increasing, with slope c>0. Write V=|D|.
The actual H-buffered maximal raw depth Q satisfies

    Q>=Gamma_d ell(b)^d V.                             (1)

Indeed the ordinary centroid of K_b has own-fiber cap mass at least
Gamma_d|K_b|, hence at least that ambient mixed cap mass. Buffered
depth only increases each through-mark cap.

At the actual deepest mark over a, choose opposite continuous cap
directions and a sufficiently large base tilt toward z<a. Every
fiber z<a is fully included and every z>a excluded. On the own fiber
the two buffered caps cover it, with overlap contained in a slab of
width twice the buffer displacement. The uniform section bound gives

    Q<=sum_(z<a)|K_z|+|K_a|/2+C epsilon.                (2)

Here C is a fixed finite raw-mass constant on the compact normalized
class, using f_H<=1 and the covariance bound. Without the buffer this
holds exactly with zero error. It is not valid to omit the error for
the buffered Q.

Combining (1), (2), and the envelope yields

    Gamma_d ell(b)^d
      <=sum_(z<a)ell(z)^d+ell(a)^d/2+C epsilon/V.        (3)

Let t=ell(a)/c. Positivity of ell on the complete sampled projection
means that every predecessor z=a-k has k<t. Hence the necessary
dimensionless inequality is

    Gamma_d (t+m)^d
      <=t^d/2+sum_(k=1)^(ceil(t)-1)(t-k)^d
                    +C epsilon/(V c^d).              (4)

The earlier finite-epsilon pure-base bound, which includes the entire
own fiber instead of its half, is exact without the epsilon error.
Equation (4) can be used in a limit only after retaining or controlling
its displayed scale-dependent error.

## 2. The unbuffered restriction still permits a pointwise jump above two

Take d=13, t=19 and m=2. Both strict inequalities hold:

    (13/14)^13 * 21^13
       < 19^13/2+sum_(k=1)^18 k^13,

    22^13 > 19^13+20^13+21^13.                         (5)

These have the following exact positive integer certificates:

    14^13[19^13+2 sum_(k=1)^18 k^13]
                   -2*13^13*21^13
      =809166980250791721289725405278,

    22^13-19^13-20^13-21^13
      =4364696681706232.

Thus the strengthened endpoint condition alone does not preclude an
individual next-fiber weight exceeding the sum of the three source
weights, which is the local mechanism behind a density jump greater
than two. No compatible configuration with all the actual source and
cap equations is manufactured by this numerical condition. It only
shows that those additional equations cannot be discarded after
deriving (4).
